rubrics.justification: It broadly matches the reported 3AB grade, but the image is limited and the response adds several speculative features not reliably visible (granularity, vacuolization, extracellular debris, irregular contour/degeneration), reducing morphological accuracy.
It integrates age, ovarian response, sperm, diagnosis, prior outcomes, BMI, and endometrial thickness with embryo quality and prognosis reasonably well, though some links are overstated.

The structure is logical, but several deductions are overconfident or weakly supported, including attributing prior failures mainly to receptivity, assigning precise percentage deductions, and inferring biologic effects from former smoking and stress.

While some points are standard (single good-quality blastocyst, consider uterine evaluation after repeated failures), multiple recommendations are not guideline-based or are controversial for routine use, including NK-cell testing, KIR/HLA-C, cytokine profiling, MTHFR testing, ERA as highest priority, EMMA/ALICE, aspirin/heparin without indication, and calling hysteroscopy mandatory.
The response gives clear next-step suggestions for transfer optimization and future evaluation, but some actions are too aggressive or insufficiently evidence-based for this case.
